Title: Maternal and newborn deaths and illness are reduced among women and children in Woredas Basha and Kecha, Demo Zone
Women and newborns receive quality, timely maternal and newborn health services at supported facilities and in the community
Families and communities support safe motherhood, early care-seeking and newborn care
Health workers (midwives, nurses, HEWs) competent in BEmONC, essential newborn care and integrated ANC/PNC
Supported facilities provide round-the-clock safe delivery, newborn care and referral (maternity waiting homes, referral transport)
Essential MNCH medicines and supplies are continuously available at supported facilities
Remote kebeles are reached by monthly integrated outreach clinics (ANC, PNC, immunisation)
Women's Development Army volunteers identify pregnancies early and refer
Men, women and community leaders support facility delivery and newborn care practices
Woreda health offices use MNCH data to manage services
BEmONC and essential newborn care training for midwives and nurses (two batches)
Integrated ANC/PNC and danger-sign refresher training for health extension workers
Monthly on-the-job mentoring and supportive supervision at supported facilities
Rehabilitate and equip delivery and newborn care corners at 4 health posts and 2 health centres
Operate two maternity waiting homes and the community referral transport scheme
Monthly MNCH supply forecasting, ordering and last-mile delivery
Monthly stock and cold-chain checks at supported facilities
Monthly integrated outreach clinics (ANC, PNC, immunisation) in remote kebeles
Orient and refresh WDA team leaders (1-to-5 networks) on pregnancy identification and danger signs
Kebele pregnancy mapping and referral-slip distribution with HEWs
Community education sessions through women's groups, religious leaders and husbands' forums
Radio messages and community conversations on maternal and newborn danger signs
Monthly woreda MNCH data review and action meetings
Baseline and endline MNCH coverage survey
